The San Francisco District Attorney's Office is one of the premier law enforcement organizations in the United States. Our mission is to collaborate with the City’s diverse communities and law enforcement agencies to make San Francisco one of the safest cities in America. Our office engages in public education and crime prevention efforts while maintaining the traditional role of investigating, charging, and prosecuting all criminal violations occurring within the City and County of San Francisco. The Director of Communications provides strategic leadership and direction for all internal and external communications and marketing for the Department. The ideal candidate for this position will be creative, proactive, detail\-oriented, and self\-motivated.

*Strategic Leadership*

* Serve as primary media contact and spokesperson for the department.

jobs.description:
Under the direction of the Executive Director, the Chief Operating Officer will assist the Executive Director with the overall management of the organization. This position also advises the Executive Director and Harbor Board of Trustees on policy matters that would further the mission of the organization and ensure compliance with various contractual, regulatory, legal, and other requirements related to service provision and delivery.


The Chief Operating Officer shall be responsible for the leadership, planning, organization, development, and direction of assigned departments in accordance with applicable law, the contract with the California Department of Developmental Services, and the policies established by Harbor’s Board of Trustees.


Under the general direction of the Executive Director, this position will track, monitor, and manage the organization’s compliance requirements, support the Executive Team and other agency staff members with completion of compliance requirements, and communicate with the California Department of Developmental Services and other entities as appropriate regarding compliance projects, timelines and required reports.


### **Responsibilities**


* Serves as Acting Executive Director in the absence of the Executive Director.


* Represents the Executive Director at statewide and local meetings as assigned.


* Assists in the development, implementation, and monitoring of Harbor’s strategic plan, regional center performance measures, and contractual program obligations.


* Advises the Executive Director and Harbor’s Board of Trustees on service policy, program policy, service delivery trends, and compliance matters.


* Assists the Executive Director in providing the Board of Trustees with sufficient, up\-to\-date information and with new Board members’ orientation.


* Implements Harbor’s policies and procedures.


* Provides leadership, support, and day\-to\-day supervision to assigned departments, committees, workgroups or task forces.


* Manages the follow up and communications related to recommendations from department/staff meetings and leadership team meetings held by the Executive Director and the Operations Team.


* Supports workforce planning, recruitment, and retention efforts to maintain highly skilled staff.


* Establishes performance metrics, quality standards, and data\-driven decision\-making processes to monitor program effectiveness and outcomes.


* Builds and maintains relationships with key stakeholders, including service providers and other community partner organizations.


* Fosters a culture of collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.


* Assists in the development and management of Harbor’s budget.


* Assists in the supervision and functioning of the executive office.


### **SECONDARY DUTIES**


Performs other tasks and functions as assigned by the Executive Director.


### **ENVIRONMENT/PHYSICAL ACTIVITY**


The incumbent is in a non‐confined office‐type setting in which he or she is free to move about at will. The environment for this position is mostly clean and comfortable but may include some minor annoyances such as noise, odors, drafts, etc. In addition, the incumbent may spends time in other community facilities. The incumbent will be exposed to volatile and emotional individuals and their families.


In the course of performing this work, the incumbent will also be required to travel via personal vehicle or public transportation to other facilities, group homes, service providers, and community locations as needed. The incumbent:


* Will spend time sitting, utilizing the computer.
* Will spend limited time standing/walking throughout the facilities.
* May lift up to 15 periodically. If more, the incumbent must request assistance.
* May stoop or stretch to access file cabinets, shelves.
* May be grabbed, pushed or hit by an individual receiving services.

The individual in this position may operate any standard office equipment including telephones, copy machines, scanning equipment, postage meter, computer peripheral equipment, etc.


Computer software may include any or all of the following:


* Microsoft Office including Word, Outlook, Excel, and Power Point
* VirtualCHART
* Video conferencing platforms (e.g. Zoom, Teams, etc.)

The incumbent must be able to perform this job safely, without endangering the health or safety of themselves or others. Individuals with disabilities that may impact their ability to perform these duties are encouraged to meet with Human Resources to discuss options for accommodation.


### **POSITION REQUIREMENTS**


These specifications are general guidelines based on the minimum experience normally considered essential to the satisfactory performance of this job. Individual abilities may result in some deviation from these guidelines.


### **To perform effectively in this position, the incumbent must have:**


* Ability to uphold and model Harbor’s vision, mission and guiding values in all leadership and management practices.
* Commitment to fostering a person\-centered organization and customer\-service culture.
* Ability to effectively collaborate with persons with developmental disabilities and their families; providers of services; state and local governmental agencies; advocacy organizations; legislators and their staff; and the community at large. Ability to lead and manage a multi\-million\-dollar organization. The ability to work effectively with a Board of Directors/Trustees.
* Knowledge of the principles of social service delivery; planning and organization, leadership and management; budgeting; personnel law; and Board of Directors’/ Trustees’ governance. A comprehensive knowledge of regional centers and state and federal statutes and regulations relative to the delivery of services to persons with developmental disabilities.
* Ability to work collaboratively as a team member and across the organization to build and foster teams.
* Adaptable multitasker

**About the Environment program**
---------------------------------



Launched 40 years ago, the Mott Foundation’s Environment program has long supported programs around the world that protect communities and the ecosystems upon which they depend. This work has demonstrated that such grantmaking must seek practical ways to build strong economic, social and environmental conditions for all people — in a word, sustainability. In 2025, the Environment program awarded 93 grants totaling more than $20 million.



This is an exciting time to join the Environment team as they begin to implement in 2026 a new 10\-year program plan. Based on the lessons learned from their long\-term engagement in the field, the team will pursue three initiatives:


* One Water, which will promote clean, affordable and accessible water for all from source to tap, both in the Great Lakes region and across the United States.
* Finance for Sustainability, which aims to influence international finance to drive the transition to low\-carbon energy, protect ecosystems and uphold the rights of local communities.
* Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin, which will work to advance land rights, ecological stewardship and sustainable livelihoods in the Amazon basin.

**The opportunity**
-------------------



The Mott Foundation is seeking a program director to lead its Environment program at an important moment in its evolution. With a new 10\-year plan underway and an anticipated investment of $200 million across its three initiatives, the incoming director will help translate an ambitious strategy into meaningful, durable results.



At its core, the role requires understanding the breadth of the Environment program well enough to provide sound oversight, communicate the work clearly to Foundation leadership and trustees, and create the conditions for talented program officers to deploy resources effectively. The program director will lead primarily through judgment, coaching, inquiry and influence, while also ensuring that the program’s grantmaking and internal processes are executed with consistency and excellence.
